nodes.title: Story 2.1: Doctor Login with OpenMRS Credentials
nodes.description: P0 story for Epic 2 (Authentication & Session Management). Implements doctor login using OpenMRS REST API session endpoint. Creates auth service (login() in src/services/api/auth.ts), AuthContext (src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx) for session management, login screen UI (src/app/index.tsx) with Material Design 3 and OpenMRS O3 theme, login flow connecting form to AuthContext with SecureStore token storage, and protected route wrapper (src/app/(auth)/_layout.tsx) that redirects unauthenticated users.

nodes.title: Story 2.2: Handle Invalid Login Credentials
nodes.description: P0 story for Epic 2. Implements clear error message display when doctor enters invalid credentials. Wires 401 error handling into login screen using mapErrorToUserMessage from @/utils/errorHandler. Ensures fields remain editable after failed login, clears error state on user interaction, and overrides generic 401 message with context-specific 'Invalid username or password. Please try again.'

nodes.title: Story 2.3: Handle Network Errors During Login
nodes.description: P1 story for Epic 2. Implements helpful message when login fails due to network issues. Distinguishes network errors (no error.response) from auth errors (401) using ErrorType.NETWORK_ERROR. Adds Retry button that reuses existing credentials. Clears network error state on user interaction or new login attempt.

nodes.title: Story 2.4: Automatic Session Timeout After 30 Minutes of Inactivity
nodes.description: P0 security story (NFR9) for Epic 2. Implements 30-minute inactivity timer in AuthContext using useRef for setTimeout handle. Adds startInactivityTimer, resetInactivityTimer, and handleSessionExpiry functions. Exposes resetInactivityTimer and sessionExpiredMessage via AuthContext. Wires interaction tracking in authenticated layout using TouchableWithoutFeedback and navigation event listeners. Includes 7 AI review follow-up patches.

nodes.title: Story 2.5: Prevent Screenshots on Clinical Screens
nodes.description: P0 security story (NFR10) for Epic 2. Enables screenshot prevention on all authenticated screens using expo-screen-capture. Applies FLAG_SECURE on (auth)/_layout.tsx level covering all child screens. Login screen is intentionally excluded. Includes AI review fixes switching from hook to imperative API guarded by isAuthenticated.

nodes.title: Story 2.6: Doctor Logout with Confirmation
nodes.description: P1 story (FR22, UX-DR18) for Epic 2. Adds logout confirmation dialog on the dashboard. Implements logout menu button in header, Android back button interception to show logout dialog instead of navigating back, confirmation dialog with Yes/No actions, and confirmed logout flow calling AuthContext.logout(). Includes AI review fixes for logout error handling and dialog dismissal guards.

nodes.title: Story 2.7: Session Persistence Across App Restarts
nodes.description: P0 story (NFR8) for Epic 2. Stores session timestamp on login in SecureStore (sessionTimestamp) alongside sessionToken and sessionUser. Validates session age on app launch in AuthContext.checkSession() - restores session if within 30 minutes, clears and shows expiry message if expired. Includes review findings for orphaned SecureStore key cleanup and defensive state reset.

nodes.title: Story 2.8: [BUG] Login Fails on First Attempt with 'An error occurred'
nodes.description: P0 bug story for Epic 2. Reports that login fails on first attempt after app launch/restart but succeeds on second attempt. Likely root causes include API client initialization race condition, AuthContext mount + SecureStore read conflict, error misclassification, or stale closure in login button handler. Status is ready-for-dev with investigation and fix tasks defined.

nodes.title: Story 3.1: View List of Assigned Patients
nodes.description: Core story for Epic 3 (My Patients Dashboard). Extends SessionResponse type to capture currentProvider for patient filtering. Creates getActiveVisits() in src/services/api/patients.ts, TypeScript types for Visit/Patient entities, usePatients SWR hook with 5-min cache and client-side filtering (active visits where doctor is provider), PatientCard component with Material Design 3 styling, and full dashboard screen in src/app/(auth)/dashboard.tsx with loading/error/empty/loaded states.

nodes.title: Story 3.2: Refresh Patient List
nodes.description: Story for Epic 3. Extends usePatients hook to expose isRefreshing state derived from SWR's isValidating. Adds pull-to-refresh using RefreshControl on FlatList and refresh IconButton in dashboard header. No new files - all changes are modifications to existing files.

nodes.title: Story 3.3: Handle Empty Patient List
nodes.description: Story for Epic 3. Already implemented ahead-of-schedule in Story 3.1. The dashboard has EmptyState with icon='account-group' and message='No active patients assigned to you'. No patient cards are rendered when list is empty. Primary task is verification and one additional test.

nodes.title: Story 3.4: Navigate to Patient Clinical Summary
nodes.description: Story for Epic 3. Creates navigation destination src/app/(auth)/patient/[id].tsx (placeholder Clinical Summary screen). Removes 'as never' cast in dashboard.tsx now that typed route exists. PatientCard already has onPress wired to router.push('/patient/${uuid}') with ripple effect from react-native-paper Card.

nodes.title: Story 3.5: Display Last Updated Timestamp
nodes.description: Story for Epic 3. Updates usePatients hook to track lastUpdatedAt using useState and useEffect with SWR's isValidating. Displays 'Last updated: X min ago' below the header using date-fns formatDistanceToNow. Auto-updates every 60 seconds via setInterval. No timestamp shown during loading or error states.

nodes.title: Story 3.6: Handle Network Errors on Dashboard
nodes.description: P1 story for Epic 3. Adds ErrorState UI when usePatients returns error. Uses mapErrorToUserMessage for context-dependent messages: network error shows 'Unable to load patients. Tap to retry.' with retry button wired to mutate(). Server errors show 'Unable to load patients. Please try again later.' with retry button. Status: done.

nodes.title: Story 4.1: View Patient Demographics
nodes.description: Core story for Epic 4 (Clinical Summary & Patient Data). Creates useClinicalSummary hook with SWR (no cache), getPatientDemographics API service calling GET /patient/{uuid}?v=full, PatientDemographics type, DemographicsCard component (outlined card with Name, ID, Age, Gender), and replaces placeholder [id].tsx with full Clinical Summary screen with loading skeleton, error state with retry, and demographics display. Reuses existing helper functions (resolveDisplayName, resolvePatientId, resolveAge).

nodes.title: Story 4.2: View Active Medications
nodes.description: Story for Epic 4. Creates Medication type in src/types/clinical.ts, getActiveMedications API calling GET /order with patient/careSetting/status filters, useMedications SWR hook, and MedicationCard component with light blue background, medication icon, drug name/dosage/frequency display, and 'No active medications recorded' empty state. Updates Clinical Summary screen to render MedicationCard below DemographicsCard.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand the project's purpose and architecture. This monorepo contains 9 OpenMRS 3.x frontend microfrontends (service queues, appointments, bed management, patient registration, patient search, ward, active visits, patient lists, home dashboard) and a React Native mobile doctor app. Each microfrontend is an independently deployable module that integrates into the OpenMRS 3.x shell via routes and extensions.

tour.title: Service Queues App — Entry Point & Configuration
tour.description: The most actively developed package. Its entry point registers routes, extensions, and dashboard links. The config schema defines customizable column definitions and table layouts. The root component sets up the React tree, and types define the core data model (VisitQueueEntry, MappedVisitQueueEntry, service/status/priority enums). The routes.json maps URL paths to component registrations.

tour.title: Service Queues App — Core Components & Hooks
tour.description: The queue table (main view) renders paginated, filterable patient lists with columns for priority, status, wait time, and actions. The default queue table shows all entries, while the by-status view groups by queue status. SWR-based hooks fetch queue entries, queues, and individual entry data. Modals handle add/move, transition, edit, delete, and call operations. A Zustand store manages selected queue location and service filters. The metrics container shows waiting patients, checked-in counts, and average wait time.

tour.title: Service Queues App — Admin, Current/Past Visit, & Create Queue Entry
tour.description: Admin pages manage queues and queue rooms with add/edit/delete forms. The create-queue-entry workspace provides a form to add patients to a queue, with existing-visit selection and queue location/service/priority fields. Current visit summary shows vitals, biometrics, and triage notes. Past visit summary shows encounter lists, medications, and notes for completed visits.

tour.title: Appointments App — Scheduling & Calendar
tour.description: The appointments microfrontend manages patient appointment scheduling. The header component provides navigation and date context. The homepage tile shows appointment counts/metrics. Calendar views display monthly workload distribution. Appointment forms handle create/edit/delete. Location-select options filter by service location. The appointments resource provides data fetching hooks for scheduled and unscheduled appointments.

tour.title: Bed Management App — Admission & Bed Tracking
tour.description: The bed management microfrontend handles ward bed allocation, administration, and tracking. The summary view shows admission locations with bed layouts, grouped by ward. Bed administration provides CRUD tables for beds, bed types, and bed tags. The bed form workspace validates bed creation/editing with tag and type assignments. Types define Bed, BedTag, BedType, and BedPostPayload interfaces. Resource hooks fetch admission locations, bed layouts, tags, and types using SWR.

tour.title: Patient Registration App — Registration Workflow
tour.description: The patient registration microfrontend handles new patient creation and editing. The form manager orchestrates multi-section registration with validation, offline queuing, and patient ID generation. Field components support name, address (with search/lookup), date of birth, and identifier inputs. Demographics and death-info sections compose these fields. The add-patient link extension provides a quick-register entry point from the patient search context.

tour.title: Patient Search App — Search & Patient Banners
tour.description: The patient search microfrontend provides compact and advanced search interfaces. The search bar allows quick patient lookup by name or ID. The advanced search page supports filtering by name, ID, location, and other attributes with paginated results. The patient banner component displays key patient info (name, age, gender, ID) with a start-visit button. The search page component orchestrates the overall search experience with views for compact and full-width layouts.

tour.title: Ward App — Inpatient Management
tour.description: The ward microfrontend provides comprehensive inpatient management. The ward view displays beds grouped by location with patient occupancy indicators. Ward patient cards show patient info, identifiers, and relationships. The header shows admission requests and ward metrics (empty beds, patients, admissions). Workspaces handle patient admission, discharge, transfer, bed swap, and clinical note-taking. Hooks manage data fetching for admission locations, beds, inpatient requests, EMR configuration, and patient observations.

tour.title: Active Visits App — Visit Tracking & Summaries
tour.description: The active visits microfrontend tracks currently active patient visits across the facility. The active visits table shows visit details with configurable columns for encounters, observations, and identifiers. Visit detail components show encounters, medications, notes, and test results grouped by visit. The home page tiles display active visit counts and total visit metrics. Resource hooks fetch active visits with sorting, pagination, and observation concept metadata.

tour.title: Mobile App (ghc-ai-doctor-app) — React Native Doctor App
tour.description: The React Native mobile application for doctors provides on-the-go patient management. The API client module handles HTTP communication with the OpenMRS backend, including auth, patient lookup, and clinical data retrieval. Custom hooks encapsulate fetching patients, clinical summaries, allergies, vitals, medications, and conditions. Screens include patient list, patient detail, vitals, medications, chat, login, signup, settings, and about. Types define the mobile data model for patients, visits, assessments, clinical data, and navigation routing.

tour.title: Shared Infrastructure — Mocks, Test Utilities, & E2E Tests
tour.description: Shared test infrastructure supports all microfrontends. Mock files (patients, visits, queue entries, appointments, locations, etc.) provide reusable test fixtures. The test-utils module supplies helpers for rendering with context, router, SWR, and i18n. E2E page objects and specs using Playwright cover service queues, appointments, bed management, patient registration, ward admission/discharge, and patient search. Setup-tests configures Jest with i18n mocking and react-testing-library.
